hero.lead: A nation of 112.8 million that mines three-quarters of the world’s cobalt and keeps three-fifths of its land under forest, and still connects fewer than one in four citizens to electricity.

capital.heading: DR Congo has entered the bond market. Now the cobalt must pay for the classroom.

record.text: Debut Eurobond, April 2026: 2032 at a yield of 8.75% and 2037 at 9.50%, with investor interest above $5 billion
Public debt of about 18% of GDP in 2025; the IMF assesses a moderate risk of external and overall debt distress
IMF Extended Credit Facility, approved January 2025; third review completed 26 June 2026
International reserves, end-March 2026, slightly below three months of imports
World Bank IDA credit, first phase of the $1 billion Inga 3 Development Program, approved 3 June 2025

register.name: Debut Eurobond, dual tranche
register.detail: Announced 9 April 2026 · 2032 at a yield of 8.75% · 2037 at a yield of 9.50%
register.note: Investor interest above $5 billion across both tranches
register.text: The nation’s first international bond, in a five-year and a ten-year tranche, with investor interest of more than four times the amount raised. It opens a new source of long-term finance for the public budget that carries the seven standards.
by: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

register.name: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience, Ebola additional financing
register.detail: Announced 13 October 2026 · Additional financing
register.note: With $13 million for preparedness in 11 countries of the region
register.text: Additional financing for the national Ebola response led by the Government. It strengthens disease surveillance, laboratory capacity, clinical case management, infection control and community engagement, so that an outbreak is contained before it reaches the health standard of the whole nation.

register.name: Investment Facilitation Project
register.detail: Approved 23 July 2026 · IDA credit
register.note: Feasibility studies and a Pre-Investment Fund
register.text: Pays for feasibility and environmental and social studies for priority projects in agriculture, energy, transport and water, makes the national Pre-Investment Fund operational and trains public investment staff. It turns the projects behind the food, water and energy standards into investments ready to finance.

register.name: Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery, Phase 3
register.detail: Approved 1 July 2026 · IDA credit · with $50 million of commercial financing
register.note: Funds arranged in advance for climate and other shocks
register.text: Joins DR Congo to a Regional Climate Risk Fund, managed by African Risk Capacity, that holds reserves, contingent financing and insurance for shocks, with funds meant to reach the finance ministry within seven days. Money ready before a flood or drought protects food and livelihood when they are most at risk.

register.name: DRC Multisectoral Nutrition and Health Project, 2026 financing
register.detail: Approved 25 June 2026 · World Bank Finances One · project first financed in 2019
register.note: Nutrition services for young children and mothers
register.text: New World Bank financing for a project, first financed in 2019, that aims to increase the use of nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions. It targets children up to 23 months old and pregnant and lactating women, for the food and health standards.

register.name: Kinshasa Urban Transformation and Jobs Program (Kin la Belle), Phase 1
register.detail: Approved 28 April 2026 · IDA credit
register.note: Waste management and jobs in a city of more than 17 million
register.text: Builds collection points, transfer stations and an integrated waste management centre in Kinshasa, where 98% of the 12,000 tonnes of waste produced each day is dumped or burned. It also creates work for women and young people through public works and small firms in the waste trade, for the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Mai-Ndombe emission reductions payment
register.detail: Paid June 2025 · 3.89 million tonnes of emissions reduced · first payment under an agreement of up to $55 million
register.note: Forest Carbon Partnership Facility
register.text: A payment for reducing emissions from deforestation in Mai-Ndombe province. Under a benefit-sharing plan, the money goes to local communities, Indigenous Peoples, customary authorities and local partners, so that the standing forest pays a livelihood.

register.name: Inga 3 Development Program, first phase
register.detail: Approved 3 June 2025 · IDA credit · first phase of a $1 billion programme
register.note: About 100 communities, 1.2 million people, near Inga
register.text: The first phase of a $1 billion programme for Inga 3. It begins with the communities living close to Inga in Kongo Central: clean water, distributed renewable energy, rural roads and skills for the jobs Inga will create, for the water, energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved 15 January 2025 · 38 months · third review completed 26 June 2026
register.note: About $1.03 billion disbursed by June 2026
register.text: Supports macroeconomic stability, the business climate, governance and transparency, and inclusive growth.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: Approved 15 January 2025 · second review completed 26 June 2026
register.note: 75 percent of quota
register.text: Supports climate adaptation and mitigation, the protection of the rainforest, and the nation’s role in the low-carbon transition.

register.name: DRC Digital Transformation Project
register.detail: Announced 27 June 2024 · IDA credit · financing agreement signed November 2024 · closing 31 December 2029
register.note: With €100 million of co-financing from AFD
register.text: Part of the Inclusive Digitalization in Eastern and Southern Africa Program, it aims to increase inclusive access to and use of the internet and to strengthen the foundations for digitally enabled services. Affordable connections carry payments, learning and public services to more citizens, for the livelihood and education standards.

register.name: Water Supply and Sanitation Access Program (PASEA)
register.detail: Approved 9 June 2023 · IDA credit
register.note: Basic drinking water for 2.9 million people
register.text: Aims to provide 2.9 million people with access to basic drinking water services in the provinces of Kasai, Kasai Central, Kasai Oriental and Kwilu, for the water standard.

register.name: Forest and Savanna Restoration
register.detail: Approved 2 June 2023 · $290 million IDA credits · $10 million ESMAP Clean Cooking Fund grants
register.note: Up to 1.2 million people; 640,000 hectares
register.text: Aims to improve livelihoods and resilience for up to 1.2 million people and to bring 640,000 hectares of land under sustainable management practices. A forest that pays its communities serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Girls’ Learning and Empowerment Project
register.detail: Approved 28 March 2023 · IDA
register.note: Secondary schools, with a focus on keeping girls in school
register.text: Strengthens the quality of and access to secondary schools, with a special focus on keeping adolescent girls in school, in the provinces with the lowest participation of girls. It is aimed at the standard that holds the nation lowest.

register.name: Stabilization and Recovery in Eastern DRC Project
register.detail: Announced 20 December 2022 · IDA grant
register.note: 3.3 million people in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu
register.text: Finances community-based stabilization, community-based reintegration and the decentralization of governance for 3.3 million Congolese in the eastern provinces of Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu, with indirect benefits for the 17 million people who live there.

register.name: Transport and Connectivity Support Project
register.detail: Approved 23 June 2022 · IDA · 440 km of roads in Kasai and North Kivu
register.note: First of three projects linking Kasai and the east
register.text: Upgrades and paves 440 kilometres of climate-resilient roads in the Kasai and North Kivu provinces, lays fibre optic cable along them and supports governance of the sector. Roads that stay open carry food to market and children to school.

register.name: Empowering Women Entrepreneurs and Upgrading MSMEs for Economic Transformation and Jobs (TRANSFORME DRC)
register.detail: Approved 2 May 2022 · IDA · seven cities
register.note: Additional financing of $200 million sought in April 2026
register.text: Supports the creation of up to 2,500 formal firms, capabilities and market access for up to 25,000 women entrepreneurs and access to finance for up to 5,000 established micro, small and medium enterprises in Bukavu, Bunia, Goma, Kananga, Kinshasa, Matadi and Mbuji-Mayi. It is to contribute to a projected 28,000 jobs, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Access Governance and Reform for the Electricity and Water Sectors Project
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2022 · IDA · $34 million of Green Climate Fund grants planned in addition
register.note: Electricity and water together
register.text: Aims to expand access to renewable-based electricity and drinking water in selected urban and peri-urban areas, improve the commercial performance of the electricity and water utilities and strengthen selected provincial and national institutions, for the energy and water standards.

register.name: Enhancing Collection of Revenue and Expenditure Management (ENCORE) Project
register.detail: Approved 16 December 2021 · $125 million grant · $125 million credit
register.note: Mining revenue transparency
register.text: Aims to increase the transparency of mining revenue, bring more of it to the Treasury and strengthen expenditure management at the centre and in selected provinces, so that more of the mining revenue reaches the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Crisis Response Project for Affected Populations in Eastern DR Congo (PRECAPE)
register.detail: Announced 29 April 2026 · $33.91 million loan · $4.95 million Transition Support Facility grant · $9.97 million African Development Fund grant
register.note: More than 800,000 people in Uvira, Beni and Walikale
register.text: Rebuilds and equips seven schools, seven health facilities, five vocational training centres, water and sanitation systems and markets for displaced people and their host communities in North and South Kivu. It restores education, health, water and livelihood at once in the provinces most affected by conflict.

register.name: Connectivity of the Ngandajika Agro-Industrial Park
register.detail: Announced 8 December 2025 · Loan · total cost $177.16 million with the Government
register.note: Roads to the park and the Mbuji-Mayi airport runway
register.text: Upgrades the roads that link the Ngandajika agro-industrial park to National Roads 1 and 2 and extends the Mbuji-Mayi airport runway for farm freight. It connects farmers in the Kasai region to buyers, for the food and livelihood standards.
by: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

register.name: Project to Support the Development of Value Chains (PADCV-PTA)
register.detail: Announced 18 July 2024 · $250.4 million African Development Fund loan · $10 million Transition Support Facility loan · total cost $311.6 million
register.note: 295,000 hectares of maize, soya, cassava and rice in six provinces
register.text: Part of the Agriculture Transformation Programme, it lifts production of the main staple crops in Kongo Central, Kwango, Mai-Ndombe, Kasai Oriental, Lomami and South Kivu. About 900,000 farming households, including displaced people, are to benefit directly, for the food and livelihood standards.
by: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

register.name: Agribusiness and jobs partnership
register.detail: Signed 16 April 2026, Kinshasa · trust fund to December 2029
register.note: UK contribution to an IFC programme
register.text: A contribution from the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to a four-year IFC programme in DR Congo. It aims to support more than 300 women-owned small firms and to improve access to equipment and finance for at least 5,000 farmers and agribusinesses, for the food and livelihood standards.
by: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

register.name: Baobab DRC, loan for small businesses
register.detail: Approved 30 June 2026 · senior loan · 3 years
register.note: At least a quarter for firms led or owned by women
register.text: A loan of up to $5 million to Baobab DRC, a microfinance institution founded in 2013, to be lent on only to micro, small and medium enterprises. Credit for small firms builds a steadier livelihood for their owners and workers.

register.name: Airtel Congo RDC, loan for the mobile network
register.detail: Approved 18 June 2026 · signed 25 June 2026 · invested 16 July 2026 · A loan
register.note: Part of up to $150 million of IFC senior debt for Airtel Africa subsidiaries in DR Congo and Kenya
register.text: An IFC loan to Airtel Congo RDC to support an accelerated expansion of its mobile network across DR Congo and to refinance existing debt. It is expected to strengthen access to quality mobile connectivity through more capacity and wider coverage, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Eastcastle Infrastructure DRC, shared telecom towers
register.detail: Approved 15 June 2026 · signed 16 July 2026 · invested 25 August 2026 · loan
register.note: With a concessional blended facility of up to $29 million
register.text: A loan to a company that owns and operates shared mobile towers in DR Congo, to expand their capacity for mobile operators. Wider mobile coverage carries payments, prices and services to people far from a bank or a city, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Rawbank, financing for small and medium enterprises
register.detail: 4 March 2026 · $165 million senior loan arranged by IFC · $100 million risk-sharing facility
register.note: IFC $50m, Proparco $50m, BII $25m, eco.business Fund $20m, OPEC Fund $20m
register.text: A package that lets Rawbank lend more to small and medium enterprises, with the eco.business Fund share kept for farm businesses. More credit for small firms means more jobs and more food grown and sold, for the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Guarantee for the Nuru solar metro-grids
register.detail: June 2024 · guarantee to Congo Energy Solutions Limited for its investment in Nuru
register.note: Up to 15 MW of metro-grid capacity in the east
register.text: A MIGA guarantee that covers an investor in Nuru’s solar-hybrid metro-grids in eastern DR Congo, which are to serve more than 28,000 households and businesses. It brings electricity to towns the national grid does not reach, for the energy standard.

register.name: Nuru Series B equity
register.detail: Closed July 2023 · Series B equity · 13.7 MWp to be built in Goma, Kindu and Bunia
register.note: Investors include IFC, GEAPP, REPP and Proparco
register.text: More than $40 million of Series B equity for Nuru to start building 13.7 MWp of solar metrogrids in Goma, Kindu and Bunia, in the east, where the national grid does not reach, for the energy standard.

register.name: Equity BCDC, portfolio guarantee for loans to small firms
register.detail: Signed May 2023 · EURIZ portfolio guarantee · denominated in US dollars
register.note: With support from the European Union and the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States
register.text: A Proparco portfolio guarantee to support Equity BCDC’s loans to small and medium enterprises, especially those owned by women and young adults. It lets the bank lend more to the firms that create jobs, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Clean cooking working capital
register.detail: UNCDF concessional loan · CAFI-funded programme
register.note: Unlocked $18 million of follow-on private debt
register.text: Working capital for ALTECH, a Congolese distributor of clean cookstoves and solar products, now with more than 3,500 sales agents and over 400,000 products sold.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Cobalt
items.label: Mined in 2025, of 310,000 t worldwide
items.text: About three-quarters of world output, and 6 million tonnes of reserves, half the world total.
items.alt: Cobalt ore in the Katanga copperbelt

items.name: Inga
items.label: Hydropower potential at the Inga site
items.text: Inga 3 alone could generate 3,000 to 11,000 MW, depending on its design.
items.alt: Rapids on the lower Congo River at Inga

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: About 1.39 million km² of forest, the heart of the Congo Basin.

items.name: The River
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person, 2022
items.text: Abundant water, while safely managed drinking water reaches only 12% of people.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: A young nation, 45% of it in cities.

items.name: Virunga Origins
items.text: Chocolate made at the source, in Mutwanga, from cocoa grown by smallholders around Virunga National Park.

items.name: Maison Mbungu et Frère
items.text: Solar-pumped boreholes and smart meters paid by mobile money, for households in Kinshasa.

items.name: Virunga Energies
items.text: Hydropower in North Kivu: 42 MW from four plants, serving more than 35,000 customers.

items.name: ALTECH
items.text: Clean cookstoves and solar products sold by more than 3,500 agents, reaching about five million people.

items.name: Schoolap
items.text: Certified lessons online for 6,000 partner schools and 105,000 teachers, built in Kinshasa.

items.name: Panzi Hospital
items.text: A general hospital in Bukavu, founded by Dr Denis Mukwege in 1999, that cares for survivors of sexual violence and delivers more than 2,800 babies a year.

items.name: Baobab DRC
items.text: A microfinance institution founded in 2013 that lends to micro, small and medium enterprises; IFC approved a loan of up to $5 million in June 2026 to be lent on to them.

coverage.gap_text: Of Congolese children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019. Education is the standard furthest from reach.

guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 82% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: Safely managed drinking water; 36% have at least basic water

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 78% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 5% cook cleanly; 22.5% have electricity, about 124 kWh a person a year

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 3% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school; dated

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$3.00 a day; 85% live below it; dated
